sources.citation: game-design: a plain screwdriver drives a terminal screw but has no torque setting, so the torque it applies is a seeded spread around the terminal's marked value (plan D8, ADR 0015), and it opens knockouts, pryouts and box clamps (the ENTRY_TYPES registry). No size limit: driving a screw doesn't depend on the conductor.

A two-tip electrician's screwdriver with a slotted blade (ISO 2380, cited by number; a 1/4 in blade is about 1.2 x 6.5 mm) and a #2 cross-recess tip (ISO 8764, cited by number). Only the tip forms are modelled; their sizes are names.
